modules.title: Scenario-based AI workload selection
modules.summary: Deepens AI-901 workload coverage with practical business scenarios for choosing prediction, classification, anomaly detection, language, speech, vision, extraction, generative AI, and agents.

lessons.title: Choose the right AI workload for the problem
lessons.summary: Practice reading scenario clues and mapping them to common AI workloads such as prediction, classification, anomaly detection, NLP, speech, vision, extraction, generative AI, and agents.
learningObjectives: Map inputs and outputs to prediction, classification, extraction, vision, speech, or language workloads
Distinguish anomaly detection, sentiment, OCR, summarization, and agent scenarios
Choose generative AI when a solution must create grounded content or responses
lessons.explanation:
A good AI architect starts like a detective. Before choosing a model or tool, ask: **What is the input? What output or action does the business need?** Relecloud receives photos, reviews, invoices, voice calls, and telemetry, and each source points to a different workload.

Use **prediction** for a numeric or future estimate, such as demand. Use **classification** when the answer is a category, such as billing or safety. Use **anomaly detection** when the goal is to find unusual patterns. Written comments use **text analysis** such as named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and summarization. Spoken input starts with **speech to text**; spoken output uses **text to speech**. Images use **computer vision** for OCR, tags, captions, or object detection. Documents, forms, images, audio, and video that must become structured fields use **information extraction**.

Choose **generative AI** when the solution creates or transforms content. Choose an **agentic AI** pattern when the system must reason over instructions and use tools, such as checking booking rules and opening a support ticket. The skill is spotting scenario clues and selecting the workload that solves the business problem responsibly.

terminology.definition: Estimating a future or numeric outcome from patterns in data.
Assigning an item to one or more categories.
Identifying observations that are unusual compared with expected behavior.
Finding entities such as people, places, organizations, dates, and quantities in text.
A pattern where a model follows instructions and can use tools or knowledge to complete a task.

lessons.businessScenario: Relecloud wants one intake experience for travel disruptions. Customers can type complaints, upload receipts, speak to a kiosk, or share luggage photos. The team maps each requirement to the simplest workload before prototyping.
lessons.technicalExample: A decision matrix maps `receipt image -> OCR + extraction`, `call recording -> speech to text + summarization`, `review text -> sentiment + NER`, `refund spike -> anomaly detection`, and `policy-grounded reply -> generative AI with retrieval`.

misconception.myth: A generative model is always the best answer because it can handle many inputs.
misconception.reality: Generative AI is powerful, but specialized workloads can be easier to test, govern, and explain for classification, OCR, speech transcription, or field extraction.

lessons.examTakeaway: Watch for verbs: **predict**, **classify**, **detect unusual**, **extract**, **transcribe**, **synthesize**, **caption**, **summarize**, or **act with tools**. The verb often reveals the workload.
lessons.recap: Start with input and outcome. Match text to language, audio to speech, images to vision, forms and media to extraction, and content creation or tool use to generative or agentic AI.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Think of AI workloads like stations in a workshop. A saw, drill, and paintbrush all help build things, but you choose the station that matches the job.
lessons.anotherExample: Alpine Ski House inspects sensor readings, classifies incident reports, and answers policy questions: anomaly detection for sensors, classification for reports, and a grounded assistant for policy answers.

data.instructions: Name the workload before reading the answer.

items.prompt: A customer speaks into a kiosk.
items.answer: Speech to text first, then language understanding or response generation.

items.prompt: A camera sees a damaged suitcase tag.
items.answer: Computer vision with OCR, possibly followed by extraction.
